thread.title: Weekly Market Preview: Apple’s WWDC, Earnings, And More

author: Richard Saintvilus
title: Weekly Market Preview: Apple’s WWDC, Earnings, And More
text:
Shutterstock photo Thanks to a strong jobs report, the Dow Jones Industrial Average closed more than 200 points higher Friday. The U.S. economy added 223,000 jobs in May, topping expectations by about 18%. Economists polled by Reuters expected a gain of 188,000. In response, the Dow gained 219.37 points, closing 0.9% higher, while S&P 500 index added 1.08%. With a 1.5% gain, the Nasdaq was the biggest winner, lead by increased in all the FANGs — Facebook ( FB ), Amazon ( AMZN ), Netflix ( NFLX ) and Google parent Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ).
Apple ( AAPL ), meanwhile, closed at an all-time high of $190.24, putting its market cap at $935 billion, or less than 7% away from $1 trillion. The excitement is due to the company’s Worldwide Developers Conference (WWDC), which kicks off on Monday, June 4. Previews of new software features for the iPhone, Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV and iPad are among the expected announcements investors and analysts are will be looking for. There are also high expectations for Apple’s dive into augmented reality and its efforts in digital health.
Next week also features Tesla’s ( TSLA ) annual shareholders event, which kicks off on Tuesday. Needham analyst Rajvindra Gill on Friday initiated coverage on the electric-car maker with a Hold rating, saying Tesla faces "substantial manufacturing problems" with its Model 3 sedan. Gill believes the company is unlikely to reach full production rates until a year from now. This is one of several headline topics Tesla CEO Elon Musk will address Tuesday.
Elsewhere, investors’ attention remains on earnings, which have been — by and large — exceptional during the first quarter. While the number of companies still left to report is winding down, positive top- and bottom-line results should continue to trump the so-called headline risk. As such, here are four stocks that are reporting this week to keep an eye on.
Palo Alto Networks ( PANW ) - Reports before the open, Monday, June 4
Wall Street expects EPS of 96 cents per share on revenue of $545.68 million, compared to the year-ago quarter of 61 cents per share on $431.8 million in revenue.
What to Watch : New product launches for both network and cloud-based applications have strengthened Palo Alto’s revenue which grew in more than 28% year over year in Q2, despite intense competition from the likes of Check Point ( CHKP ), Cisco ( CSCO ) and Fortinet ( FTNT ) in the firewall security market. Last week, while citing strength in its channel checks and optimism in Palo Alto’s ability to sustain its improved execution, Stifel analysts raised Palo Alto’s price target from $200 to $240, suggesting a 15% upside to Friday’s closing price of $209.19.
Ambarella ( AMBA ) - Reports after the close, Tuesday, June 5
Wall Street expects Ambarella to earn 9 cents per share on revenue of $56.14 million. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earnings came to 39 cents per share on revenue of $64.14 million.
What to Watch: Is the company finally ready to move beyond its shaky past ? The company specializes on semiconductor chips that are low-powered and able to deliver high-definition and ultra HD video compression. However its largest customer is GoPro ( GPRO ), which accounts for roughly 20% of fiscal 2017 revenues. And GoPro’s struggles have been well documented . On Tuesday analysts will want to see the extent to which Ambarella can better diversify its revenue stream and continue to decouple from GoPro.
Broadcom ( AVGO ) - Reports after the close, Thursday, June 7
Wall Street expects Broadcom to deliver EPS of $4.76 per share on revenue of $5.01 billion, compared to the year-ago quarter of $3.69 per share on $4.2 billion in revenue.
What to Watch: Recently ISI analyst C.J. Muse initiated coverage on Broadcom with an Outperform rating and a $300 twelve-month price target. This represents 17% premium to Friday’s close of $256.34. "Broadcom is a collection of twenty sticky franchise businesses with world-class margins, a dominant market-leading position in each, and an oligopoly type industry structure with strong barriers to entry and pricing power driven by differentiated value to end-customers," wrote Muse. The company’s relationship with Apple, to which it provides wireless components for iPhones, is seen as long-term catalyst.
DocuSign ( DOCU ) - Reports after the close, Thursday, June 7
Wall Street expects DocuSign to post a per-share loss of 7 cents per share on revenue of $145.72 million. This will be the company’s first earnings report since its April IPO.
What to Watch: One of the most successful IPOs of the year, DocuSign provides individuals and businesses the ability to digitize an agreement process. DocuSign competes HelloSign and Adobe ( ADBE ) Sign, among others. Still, the company boasts more than 370,000 users, including more than 300 of the Fortune 500 companies, including T-Mobile ( TMUS ), Salesforce ( CRM ), Morgan Stanley ( MS ) and Bank of America ( BAC ). While the company’s IPO has surpassed the Street’s expectations, on Thursday analysts will want to DocuSign — which lists its history of operating losses as a risk factor during its filing — to outline its path towards profitability.
